title: Three-scenario budget: headcount & pricing deltas (Q2 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet that ties headcount hiring cadence to opex and runs 3 pricing scenarios to show revenue delta + contribution margin impact. This is intentionally rough — meant for FP&A + Product to iterate before we formalize for board packet.

High-level assumptions (shared across scenarios):
- FY26 run-rate baseline (starting May 2026): ARR equivalent from hosted + dedicated + private: $78,000,000 annualized revenue run-rate (VRR).
- Unit of measure for usage-based pricing = price per 1M tokens for text generation. Base price today used in model: $20 / 1M tokens (hosted).
- Gross margin (pre-headcount COGS but post-infra): 60% at current model mix. Infra/GPU + cloud + third-party licensing accounted as cost of revenue.
- Average effective price mix: hosted 65%, dedicated 25%, private 10% of revenue. Pricing moves applied to hosted prices only; dedicated/private contracts assumed negotiated separately and have ~6–12 month lag.
- Demand elasticity (hosted) baseline: -0.6 (10% price ↑ => ~6% demand drop). This is highly uncertain; we test +/- elasticity in sensitivity.
- Hiring corps: hiring starts June 2026, ramp for each hire 3 months to full productivity. Hiring cost = fully-burdened $210k / year for senior infra/eng; $140k for mid-level; $120k for support/sales. Hiring slippage assumed 20% for conservative scenario.

Scenario definitions:
1) Conservative (low growth): No price change, slow hiring (50% of planned hires executed), 15% slower usage growth vs baseline.
2) Base (plan): +5% hosted price in Sep 2026, execute 80% of hiring plan, usage grows per plan. Elasticity = -0.6.
3) Aggressive (upsell push): +12% hosted price in Sep 2026 with targeted product bundling, execute 100% hires, usage growth accelerated; elasticity assumed -0.45 (less elastic due to bundling).

HEADCOUNT PLAN (Hires planned May–Dec 2026) - summary table (FTE and incremental run-rate comp)
Columns: Role | Planned hires | Conservative hires | Base hires | Aggressive hires | Avg fully-burdened comp
- Eng - Serving runtime | 8 | 4 | 6 | 8 | $210000
- Eng - Platform/Infra | 6 | 3 | 5 | 6 | $200000
- Product/Design | 3 | 2 | 3 | 3 | $160000
- SRE & Ops | 4 | 2 | 3 | 4 | $150000
- Sales & Solutions | 5 | 3 | 4 | 5 | $140000
- Customer Success | 4 | 2 | 3 | 4 | $120000
- Finance & Legal | 2 | 1 | 2 | 2 | $180000
Totals (incremental hires) = 32 planned -> Conservative 17, Base 26, Aggressive 32.

Estimated incremental annualized headcount cost (run-rate add to FY26):
- Conservative: sum(product of hires * comp) = approx $3.5M (rounded, slow ramp = 60% of full year effect in 2026)
- Base: approx $6.1M (80% hires, average ramping -> ~70% full-year effect)
- Aggressive: approx $7.9M (100% hires, average ramping -> ~80% full-year effect)
(Notes: these are purposely approximate; detailed per-role month-level sheet linked in linked_artifacts gsheet).

PRICING / REVENUE SENSITIVITY (hosted price changes only)
Inputs: baseline hosted revenue = 65% of VRR = $50.7M. Baseline hosted price per 1M tokens = $20.
Assume hosted usage volume baseline = X units such that price*units = $50.7M. We model price uplifts and apply elasticity to compute new volume.
Quick sensitivity table (hosted):
Columns: Scenario | Hosted price delta | Elasticity used | Volume delta (%) | New hosted rev ($M) | Revenue delta vs baseline ($M)
- Conservative | 0% | -0.6 | 0% | 50.7 | 0.0
- Base | +5% | -0.6 | -3.0% | price*(1.05)*units*(0.97) => approx 50.7 * 1.05 * 0.97 = 51.7 | +1.0
- Aggressive | +12% | -0.45 | -5.4% | 50.7 * 1.12 * 0.946 = approx 53.7 | +3.0
(Interpretation: even with elasticity hit, revenue improves with moderate uplifts because price effect > volume loss in these ranges.)

FULL COMPANY REVENUE + OPEX IMPACT (annualized view post-change, 12-month run-rate)
Start ARR baseline: $78.0M. Hosted delta flows to total ARR based on hosted mix.
- Conservative: Revenue = $78.0M (no pricing delta), incremental headcount cost +$3.5M, gross margin roughly stable but contribution margin down ~4.5% pts due to hiring.
- Base: Hosted rev +$1.0M -> total ARR ~ $79.0M. Incremental headcount cost +$6.1M. Net impact: small revenue gain, opex +6.1M -> contribution margin compressed ~6–7% pts year-over-year.
- Aggressive: Hosted rev +$3.0M -> total ARR ~ $81.0M. Incremental headcount cost +$7.9M. Net: revenue growth outpaces hiring somewhat but still margin compression ~4–5% pts (because headcount dollars frontloaded faster than revenue ramp).

Key sensitivity explored quickly (notes):
- If elasticity is higher (e.g., -1.0), Base scenario (+5%) would lose ~5% volume => net hosted rev roughly equal to baseline, removing revenue upside and leaving full cost of hires. That makes price increases risky without mitigating actions.
- If bundling reduces elasticity to -0.3 (aggressive bundling and lock-in), +12% yields stronger rev uplift (~+8% hosted rev) and helps pay for hiring more quickly.
- Hiring slippage is the biggest operational lever: conservative miss means lower opex but also slower product delivery and future revenue. A 20% slip reduces headcount cost by ~1.2M in Base, improving margin profile materially.

Short recommendations (for discussion):
- Move forward with Base price test: +5% hosted price on a time-limited rollout (T+90 days) with telemetry to measure actual elasticity across top 20 customers and self-serve cohort. Include promo controls to protect enterprise deals during negotiation windows.
- Pause full hiring for non-critical infra roles until we confirm price behavior; prioritize hires that increase unit economics (billing/ingestion engineers, caching/batching optimizers).
- Run parallel elasticity experiments by customer segment (self-serve vs enterprise) and instrument churn metrics; prepare contingency playbook in case elasticity >> -0.8.
- Prepare tiered packaging (feature + SLA) to reduce price elasticity for targeted customers and justify higher price.

Next steps / action items: 
- FP&A to produce month-level P&L with per-role ramp (linked gsheet) — deadline 2026-03-18 (Marco).
- Product to propose bundling list and enforcement plan (Sofia) — draft 2026-03-22.
- Sales ops to flag top 30 at-risk accounts from pricing change and propose mitigation credits (Ben) — initial list 2026-03-19.

Open questions / flags:
- How will Dedicated/private contract renewal cadence interact with hosted price changes? We assume ~6–12 month lag; need legal review for automatic pass-through.
- Are there regulatory or reseller channel rules that constrain list price changes for certain customers? (CS to confirm)
- Do we have telemetry to directly map token usage to customer value for enterprise customers? (Product instrumentation).

Scratch notes / quick sensitivity table (raw numbers) - do not present to board yet:
- Baseline hosted rev = $50.7M
- Base price+5% & elasticity -0.6 => new rev = 50.7 * 1.05 * (1 - 0.6*0.05)= 50.7 * 1.05 * 0.97 = ~51.7M
- Aggressive +12% & elasticity -0.45 => new rev = 50.7 * 1.12 * (1 - 0.45*0.12)= 50.7 * 1.12 * 0.946 = ~53.7M
- Sensitivity if elasticity = -1.0 and +5% => new rev = 50.7 * 1.05 * (1 - 1*0.05)= 50.7 * 1.05 * 0.95 = ~50.6M (no upside)

Bottom line (quick): moderate hosted price moves can increase revenue, but headcount cadence and elasticity uncertainty means margin impact is ambiguous. Recommend controlled +5% hosted experiment + targeted hiring prioritization.

-- end of working sheet (notes to self: convert to clean month-by-month gsheet once we lock elasticity priors)
